# Cloud Markdown↔ADF functions (pure capability; AdfCodec untouched)

## Context / Problem
Jira Cloud stores rich text as ADF (structured JSON). The `RichTextCodec` seam
(epic `e369`, story J3 / `aac8`) routes Cloud rich text through `AdfCodec`
(`adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py`), a pass-through wrapper over the pinned
`adapters/jira/adf.py`. **`adf.py`'s encode is plain-text-structured, not
Markdown-aware:** `text_to_adf` (`adf.py:275`) splits the body on blank lines and
emits each block as one `paragraph` node, so Markdown block syntax (headings, list
markers, fenced code) and inline syntax (bold/strike/link) is carried as **literal
characters** and Cloud renders raw source. Its `adf_to_text` (`adf.py:26`) already
emits Markdown-ish text on decode; the missing half is a Markdown-aware **encode**.

**Why this story ships pure functions, not a codec change.** On Cloud, codec ops
are reachable on the LIVE send path: `AdfCodec.fit_outbound` fits the description
that is posted, via `jira_fields.py:53`
(`_shared_sanitize_description(..., fit=AdfCodec().fit_outbound)`) →
`backend._JiraSanitizer.sanitize_description` → `acli.py:205`
(`_text_to_adf(_sanitize_description(value))`). The description-compare sites also
call `adf.py` directly (`outbound_fields.py:564`, `inbound_differ.py:210`). So
**repointing `AdfCodec` ops in this story would change live Cloud truncation and
comparison** — a cutover that must land together with echo-safety in `3388`
(which depends on this story), never before it. To keep capability strictly
separate from the hazardous cutover, **this story delivers only the new Markdown↔ADF
functions in `adf.py` and their tests, and leaves `AdfCodec` a plain pass-through.**
Nothing observable changes on merge.

## Prior art in this repo (the seam we build on — NOT greenfield)
- `RichTextCodec` Protocol — `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py` (four ops).
- `AdfCodec` (Cloud) — `adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py`; pass-through over
  `adf.py`, pinned by `test_rich_text_codec.py:198`
  (`test_adf_codec_is_a_pass_through_to_the_pinned_adf_module`), asserting
  `fit_outbound == adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit` (`:205`),
  `to_wire == adf.text_to_adf` (`:207`), `decode_inbound == adf.adf_to_text(...)`
  (`:208`). **Left unchanged by this story;** `3388` updates these when it repoints.
- `adf.py` — `text_to_adf` (`:275`), `adf_to_text` (`:26`),
  `normalize_description` (`:310`), `fit_text_to_adf_limit` (`:341`). New functions
  are ADDED here; the existing plain ones stay for the live path + fallback.
- Live Cloud consumers of the codec/`adf.py` (rerouted later by `3388`):
  `jira_fields.py:53` (fit), `acli.py:205` / `acli_cli_ops.py:369` (encode),
  `outbound_fields.py:564` / `inbound_differ.py:210` (compare).

## Engine decision: vendored `marklas` (committed, not a spike)
Use **`marklas`** (pure-Python, mistune-based, MIT) for Markdown↔ADF, **vendored
under `src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/` with its upstream provenance recorded**:
- Upstream: `https://github.com/byExist/marklas`; PyPI distribution `marklas`.
- Pin the exact upstream **version + commit sha in `pyproject.toml`**, and copy the
  upstream **MIT `LICENSE`** into `src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/LICENSE` (single-
  maintainer bus-factor is mitigated by vendoring a pinned copy).

This is a **committed decision backed by a completed experiment**, not an open
spike: a direct head-to-head against `adf.py` over a 5,730-body corpus (see the
fixture below) measured marklas at **99.65% idempotent round-trip** (echo-safe
under the reconciler's normalize-both-sides model) while producing
**structurally-rich ADF for 56.7%** of bodies (56.3% both rich AND idempotent).
The ≥99.6% AC below locks that measured bar in as a regression. Scripts + raw
counts: session log `5eb0-52a3-45f0-43e5`; `files/parity_*.py`,
`files/parity-results.md`.

### Rejected alternative — extend `adf.py`'s handlers in-house
Weighed and **rejected on empirical grounds** (recorded here so the review sees the
rationale). The appeal was that `adf.py`'s *decode* already emits Markdown-ish
text, suggesting a symmetric *encode* is small. The corpus head-to-head refutes
this for the half that matters — the **encode**:
- `adf.py`'s `text_to_adf` produces **0%** structurally-rich ADF over the 5,730
  bodies: it flattens **every** construct to paragraph text and emits **zero** ADF
  marks. Of the bodies marklas renders as structured ADF, `adf.py` renders **0**:
  headings (1,924), bullet lists (2,538), task lists (1,780), ordered lists (795),
  code blocks (280), tables (60), blockquotes (33), rules (72); inline marks strong
  (1,396), inline-code (2,569), em (439), strike (7), link (12) — all 0.
- `adf.py`'s 100% round-trip fidelity is therefore **trivial**: it translates no
  rich structure, so there is nothing to lose. It is a plain-text→paragraph
  encoder, not a Markdown↔ADF codec.
- Reaching marklas parity in-house means building a **full GFM→ADF parser + ADF→GFM
  serializer** — i.e. re-implementing marklas/mistune. The prior hand-rolled
  attempt stalled at **90.7%** fixed point, its residual tail being exactly the
  emphasis/mark serialization a bespoke engine gets wrong. Only the *decode* half
  overlaps; the *encode* is greenfield.

## Approach (pure functions in `adf.py`)
Add three functions to `adf.py`, wrappers over vendored marklas, **not referenced
by any `AdfCodec` op or live send path in this story**:
1. `markdown_to_adf(md: str) -> dict` — Markdown-aware ADF encode.
2. `adf_to_markdown(doc: dict) -> str` — ADF→Markdown decode, applying a
   deterministic **mark-order canonicalizer** so co-located `strong`+`strikethrough`
   (`**~~x~~**` ⇄ `~~**x~~**`) has one canonical form (the one true 2-cycle
   oscillator; without this the pair never converges).
3. `fit_markdown_to_adf_limit(md: str, *, limit=…) -> str` — length-fit that
   measures the `markdown_to_adf` serialization (so a future markdown-aware wire is
   bounded correctly).
Ship a helper that composes an idempotent round-trip
`adf_to_markdown(markdown_to_adf(t))` for the corpus test, and a **whole-codec
plain-text fallback** helper (returns the plain `adf.py` functions as a set) that
`3388` will install on conversion error — defined and unit-tested here, wired
there.

## Corpus fixture (evaluability)
The 99.65% idempotence and the rich-coverage counts are measured against a
**vendored** fixture, `tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/` (a sanitized snapshot of
the 5,730 ticket bodies, committed into the repo — NOT re-exported from a live
store at test time), so `test_cloud_corpus_idempotence` is hermetic and
reproducible in-session. The test asserts BOTH the ≥99.6% idempotent ratio AND the
body count (5,730) so the fixture cardinality is guarded.

## Explicitly OUT of scope for this story (owned by `3388`)
- Repointing the four `AdfCodec` ops to the Markdown-aware functions + installing
  the whole-codec fallback, and updating the pin test at
  `test_rich_text_codec.py:198/205/207/208`.
- Rerouting the live Cloud consumers — `jira_fields.py:53` fit,
  `acli.py:205`/`acli_cli_ops.py:369` encode, `outbound_fields.py:564` /
  `inbound_differ.py:210` compare — to the Markdown-aware functions (paired so the
  send-fit and compare-fit stay the identical transform), the once-only re-emit
  migration, the second-pass convergence proof, and rollback.
This story changes no `AdfCodec` op and no live send site, so no observable Cloud
behavior changes on merge.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira/adf.py` — add `markdown_to_adf` / `adf_to_markdown`
  (+ mark-order canonicalizer) / `fit_markdown_to_adf_limit` + the plain-fallback
  helper; existing plain functions untouched.
- `src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/` — vendored, sha-pinned copy + upstream `LICENSE`.
- `pyproject.toml` — record the vendored upstream version + sha.
- `tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/` (new) — vendored, sanitized 5,730-body corpus.
- **Guard (UNCHANGED):** `AdfCodec` and its four ops
  (`adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py`); the shared plain-text
  `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text` (ticket 21ca; also used by sibling repo
  `agentic-dev-platform`); the live sites `jira_fields.py:53`, `acli.py:205`,
  `acli_cli_ops.py:369`, `outbound_fields.py:564`, `inbound_differ.py:210` (all
  rerouted by `3388`).
- `tests/` — unit tests for the new functions + the corpus idempotence test.

## Testing (pure-function unit + fixture-corpus only — no live send)
- **Structured round trip:** heading+checklist+inline-code+link round-trips
  MD→ADF→MD to a fixed point via `markdown_to_adf`/`adf_to_markdown`, asserting ADF
  node types (`test_cloud_adf_roundtrip`).
- **Mark-order oscillation:** the two known combined strong+strikethrough bodies
  converge in ≤1 pass under `adf_to_markdown`; a permutation property test asserts
  100% convergence.
- **Fit measures the real wire:** `fit_markdown_to_adf_limit` bounds the
  `markdown_to_adf` serialization, not the plain encode
  (`test_adf_fit_measures_the_serialized_document_not_the_plain_text`).
- **Corpus idempotence:** over the vendored `tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/`, the
  round-trip is idempotent (normalize-both-sides stable, `r(r(x))==r(x)`) for
  ≥99.6% of the bodies AND the fixture holds 5,730 bodies
  (`test_cloud_corpus_idempotence`; measured 99.65%).
- **Codec untouched:** `AdfCodec` stays a plain pass-through — the existing
  `test_adf_codec_is_a_pass_through_to_the_pinned_adf_module` stays green unmodified.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `marklas` is vendored under `src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/` with its upstream
  `github.com/byExist/marklas` version + commit sha recorded in `pyproject.toml`
  and its MIT `LICENSE` copied alongside; verified by an import/provenance test
  asserting the pinned sha and the presence of the MIT license text.
- [ ] `adf.markdown_to_adf` emits Markdown-aware ADF (heading/list/code/emphasis
  nodes, not literal `#`/`-`/`**`) and `adf.adf_to_markdown` returns the source
  Markdown; verified by `test_cloud_adf_roundtrip` asserting node types and decoded
  equality.
- [ ] The combined strong+strikethrough oscillation is eliminated by the mark-order
  canonicalizer in `adf_to_markdown`; verified by the regression + permutation
  property test (100% convergence).
- [ ] `adf.fit_markdown_to_adf_limit` measures the `markdown_to_adf` serialization;
  verified by `test_adf_fit_measures_the_serialized_document_not_the_plain_text`.
- [ ] Over the vendored `tests/fixtures/cloud_adf_corpus/` the MD→ADF→MD round-trip
  is idempotent for ≥99.6% of bodies and the fixture holds 5,730 bodies; verified
  by `test_cloud_corpus_idempotence`.
- [ ] `AdfCodec` and its four ops remain a plain pass-through and the live send
  sites are unchanged by this story; verified by the existing
  `test_adf_codec_is_a_pass_through_to_the_pinned_adf_module` staying green
  unmodified (the observable cutover is `3388`).
